correctness.rationale: The root weighted-degree identity is exact. The small-degree obstruction proves weight ≥n and excludes the only possible nonconstant equality degree sequences for n≥5. Conversely degree two at every root is sufficient, and component decomposition plus labeled exponential formula proves the precise count. Direct exhaustive verification n=5..7 and an independent cycle construction n=5..9 matched; finite tests are supporting checks only.

value.rationale: The natural perfect double Italian domination problem is solved on every triangular graph of root order at least five, with a structural characterization of every optimum, a doubled-edge refined enumerator and asymptotic. This nontrivial local-to-global rigidity is not a mere substitution or recitation of the familiar 2-factor count.
